messages.subject_clean: Soybean Seed Quality
messages.body_plain:
Dr. Matias,

Hello! I am using your FIELDimageR program and am curious if you can give me some help. I am attempting to identify hard seed and permeable phenotypes using the fieldObject method. These are the differences in the types of seed:

https://www.nature.com/articles/ng.3339 <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.nature.com%2Farticles%2Fng.3339&data=04%...%40uark.edu%7C4f9e455027074b29703f08d8dda14362%7C79c742c4e61c4fa5be89a3cb566a80d1%7C0%7C0%7C637503033042185406%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C2000&sdata=%2BEKwk77q9tHY7NPeRUXVIBYFahBA34blaEHU1b3o8ww%3D&reserved=0> / link to article - picture shown as attachment

The permeable seed is wrinkled and broken up in shades of yellow - I am trying to use this to my advantage. My current method is to break the wrinkled seeds into undiscernible objects using fieldMask with the BGI index, but I have been having inconsistent results among images. I am successful at breaking up the wrinkled seeds, but the smaller seeds are sometimes not large enough to be considered objects. This makes me think that I may need some other form of indexing to complete this project.

I am curious if you have any suggestions since you are more familiar with the program and its abilities. I have attached the code that I am using and an example image.

Thank you for your time,

messages.subject: Re: Soybean Seed Quality
messages.subject_clean: Soybean Seed Quality
messages.body_plain:
Hi John,

Thank you for asking. In your case, there are some suggestions.

You have much noise in the background (e.g., plate, text, etc.). To use FIELDimageR is better to have a unique color background as suggested here (e.g., using soybeans): https://filipematias23.github.io/FIELDimageR-Workshop-5/ <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ffilipematias23.github.io%2FFIELDimageR-Workshop-5%2F&data=04%...%40uark.edu%7C4f9e455027074b29703f08d8dda14362%7C79c742c4e61c4fa5be89a3cb566a80d1%7C0%7C0%7C637503033042175449%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C2000&sdata=L8Vr3lpSctvDXZk7E%2BtY5%2BjLa%2BiZpm2ZhsklWtVPqoo%3D&reserved=0>

My suggestion is to identify the entire seed first and then extract information for each seed instead of trying to find the disease using fieldMask. With each seed information, you can try to find an "index" or "value extracted for that seed" that can be related to the disease that you are looking for.

Please, try this code:

    Obj.1<-stack("IMG_0302.jpg")

    plotRGB(Obj.1)

    Obj.1<- aggregate(Obj.1,3)

    Obj.S<-fieldPolygon(mosaic=Obj.1, extent = T)

    Test1<-fieldIndex(Obj.1, index = c("BGI","SCI","HUE",

                                      "BIM","BI","NGRDI"))

    plot(Test1$BGI) # Seems values above .8 it's background

    Obj.2<- fieldMask(mosaic = Obj.1,index = "BGI",cropValue = .8,cropAbove = T)

    Test2<-fieldIndex(Obj.2$newMosaic, index = c("BGI","SCI","HUE",

                                      "BIM","BI","NGRDI"))

    plot(Test2$BIM) # Seems values below 12 it's background (space among seeds)

    Obj.3<- fieldMask(mosaic = Obj.2$newMosaic,index = "BIM",cropValue = 12,cropAbove = F)

    Obj.D<-fieldObject(mosaic = Obj.3$mask, watershed = T, areaValue = 0, minArea = 10000, na.rm=TRUE) # Eliminate everything below 10000 (you can change this value)

    plotRGB(Obj.1)

    plot(Obj.S$fieldShape, add=T)

    plot(Obj.D$Objects, add=T, border="red")

    plot(Obj.D$Polygons, add=T, border="blue")

    plot(Obj.D$single.obj[[1]], add=T, col="yellow")

    lines(Obj.D$x.position[[1]], col="red", lty=2)

    lines(Obj.D$y.position[[1]], col="red", lty=2)

    Obj.I<- fieldIndex(mosaic = Obj.1,index = c("BGI","GLI","VARI")) # Select indices that can give you the better information about the disease per seed.

    Obj.Data<-fieldInfo(mosaic = Obj.I[[c("BGI","GLI","VARI")]], fieldShape = Obj.D$Objects, projection = F)

    Obj.Data$fieldShape@data

Let us know if that works for you.

All the best,

Filipe

messages.body_plain:
Hi Rosangela,

Thank you for asking. This error is because your shapefile and image do not have the same projection.

Projection is important when you are trying to overlay images or trying to use the same shapefile for different orthomosaics (e.g., different flights on the same field trial).

If you are using images from Lab (e.g., seeds, leaves, etc.) you can ignore the projection to extract data using fieldInfo().

In this case, the solution is to use projection=FALSE on fieldInfo().

EX1.Info<- fieldInfo(mosaic = EX1.Indices[[c("NGRDI","BGI","myIndex")]],
                     fieldShape = EX1.Shape$fieldShape,
                     buffer = 0.05,

                     n.core = 3,
                     projection=F)

Please, let me know if it workes.

All the best,
Filipe

messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

The script below seems that is working well for your image. Please, let me know if you have questions. Just one point for your attention, your mosaic (Foto.tif) still on Digital Numbers (normally with pixels' values varying from 0 to 250). Before starting any analysis or extracting data, it's important to make the radiometric calibration first to get radiance and/or reflectance (biological meaning).

#################
### FIELDimageR ###
#################

library(FIELDimageR)
library(raster)
EX1 <- stack("Foto.tif")
plotRGB(EX1)

EX1.RemSoil<-fieldMask(EX1)

EX1.Shape<-fieldShape(mosaic = EX1.RemSoil$newMosaic,ncols = 20, nrows = 50)

# Attention: Pixel values are Digital Numbers (DN) - Layers Red, Green, and Blue (from 0 to 250)
EX1.Indices<- fieldIndex(mosaic = EX1.RemSoil$newMosaic,
                         index = c("NGRDI","BGI"),
                         myIndex = c("(Red-Blue)/Green"))

plotRGB(EX1.Indices)
plot(EX1.Shape$fieldShape, add=T)

EX1.Info<- fieldInfo(mosaic = EX1.Indices[[c("NGRDI","BGI","myIndex")]],
                     fieldShape = EX1.Shape$fieldShape,
                     buffer = 0.05,
                     n.core = 3,
                     projection=F)

EX1.Info$plotValue

Hope this can help you...!!!

All the best,
Filipe

Ola Raylson,

Acredito que voce tenha que especificar a banda/layer que pretende fazer o histograma:

hist(EX$Red)
hist(EX$Green)
hist(EX$Blue)

Ao remover o background ("fundo") fieldMask() basicamente substitui os pixels por NA mas continua sendo uma imagem. Neste caso voce tambem pode fazer o histograma para cada banda/layer:

hist(EX1.RemSoil$newMosaic$Red)
hist(EX1.RemSoil$newMosaic$Green)
hist(EX1.RemSoil$newMosaic$Blue)

Nao entendi muito bem a pergunta sobre data.frame. Existem varias formas de obter data.frame no pipeline do FIELDimageR. Para objetos individuais recomendo voce olhar o script neste link: (https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P11) para imagens de drones olhar o exemplo neste link: (https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P9).

Espero que isso ajude,
Abs

messages.body_plain:
Hi Kassim,

Thank you for asking. The pixel values output from cameras/sensors normally is on Digital Numbers (8 bits channel normally are from 0 to 250). The most common analysis pathway is to transform DN to radiance by using the camera/sensor setups. For this, you need to check the manual of your platform and/or Google about the transformation equations for each band/wavelength/layer. Another solution is to contact directly the company that provided your sensor and asks for the formulas/equations.

Normally for biological research, radiance values are transformed to reflectance values to compare experiments/genotypes. Reflectance is the ratio between the incidence radiance (e.g, from the Sun) compared to the radiance reflected from the surface (e.g., plants). The variation of reflectance observed among genotypes is used to evaluate/correlate with biomass, maturity, tolerance, resistance, yield, etc. To transform radiance to reflectance you can (1) have a reflectance sensor directly connected to your Phenotyping Platform (e.g., connected to the drone) or (2) the most common is to use a reflectance panel in the field on the same day and time that you collect the data/images. These panels have some materials with known reflectance (e.g., 40%, 60%, etc.) that are used to correct pixels values.

You can read more about other methods in this paper: https://doi.org/10.3390/rs11161917

Hope this can help you.

All the best,
Filipe

Legal Raylson,

Agora entendi sua pergunta, obrigado por explicar.

Tem como sim, neste caso basta você utilizar a saída EX.Obj.D$Objects como fieldshape no momento da extração dos dados com o fieldInfo().

Observe no código abaixo. O objeto EX.Obj.D$Objects foi utilizado para extrair informação para cada objeto da imagem em um data.frame.

Me avise se era isso que você está procurando.

Grande abraço,

Filipe

##################

### FIELDimageR ###

##################

library(raster)

library(FIELDimageR)

# Uploading file (EX_Obj.tif)

EX.Obj <- stack("EX_Obj.jpg")

EX.Obj <- aggregate(EX.Obj,4)

EX.shapeFile<-fieldPolygon(EX.Obj,extent = T)

# Removing the background

EX.Obj.M<- fieldMask(mosaic = EX.Obj, index = "BGI",cropValue = 0.7,cropAbove = T)

dev.off()

# Taking measurements

EX.Obj.D<-fieldObject(mosaic = EX.Obj.M$mask, watershed = T, minArea = 0.01)

# Taking measurements

EX.Obj.D<-fieldObject(mosaic = EX.Obj.M$mask, watershed = T, minArea = 1000)

EX.Obj.I<- fieldIndex(mosaic = EX.Obj,index = c("SI","BGI","BI"))

EX.Obj.Data<-fieldInfo(mosaic = EX.Obj.I, fieldShape = EX.Obj.D$Objects, projection = F)

EX.Obj.Data$fieldShape@data

On Sat, Mar 6, 2021 at 6:10 PM fmatias <filipem...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi Kassim,
>
> Thank you for asking. The pixel values output from cameras/sensors normally is on Digital Numbers (8 bits channel normally are from 0 to 250). The most common analysis pathway is to transform DN to radiance by using the camera/sensor setups. For this, you need to check the manual of your platform and/or Google about the transformation equations for each band/wavelength/layer. Another solution is to contact directly the company that provided your sensor and asks for the formulas/equations.
>
> Normally for biological research, radiance values are transformed to reflectance values to compare experiments/genotypes. Reflectance is the ratio between the incidence radiance (e.g, from the Sun) compared to the radiance reflected from the surface (e.g., plants). The variation of reflectance observed among genotypes is used to evaluate/correlate with biomass, maturity, tolerance, resistance, yield, etc. To transform radiance to reflectance you can (1) have a reflectance sensor directly connected to your Phenotyping Platform (e.g., connected to the drone) or (2) the most common is to use a reflectance panel in the field on the same day and time that you collect the data/images. These panels have some materials with known reflectance (e.g., 40%, 60%, etc.) that are used to correct pixels values.
>
> You can read more about other methods in this paper: https://doi.org/10.3390/rs11161917
>
> Hope this can help you.
>
> All the best,
> Filipe

> On Sat, Mar 6, 2021 at 6:10 PM fmatias <filipem...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > Hi Kassim,
> >
> > Thank you for asking. The pixel values output from cameras/sensors normally is on Digital Numbers (8 bits channel normally are from 0 to 250). The most common analysis pathway is to transform DN to radiance by using the camera/sensor setups. For this, you need to check the manual of your platform and/or Google about the transformation equations for each band/wavelength/layer. Another solution is to contact directly the company that provided your sensor and asks for the formulas/equations.
> >
> > Normally for biological research, radiance values are transformed to reflectance values to compare experiments/genotypes. Reflectance is the ratio between the incidence radiance (e.g, from the Sun) compared to the radiance reflected from the surface (e.g., plants). The variation of reflectance observed among genotypes is used to evaluate/correlate with biomass, maturity, tolerance, resistance, yield, etc. To transform radiance to reflectance you can (1) have a reflectance sensor directly connected to your Phenotyping Platform (e.g., connected to the drone) or (2) the most common is to use a reflectance panel in the field on the same day and time that you collect the data/images. These panels have some materials with known reflectance (e.g., 40%, 60%, etc.) that are used to correct pixels values.
> >
> > You can read more about other methods in this paper: https://doi.org/10.3390/rs11161917
> >
> > Hope this can help you.
> >
> > All the best,
> > Filipe

> > > Hi Kassim,
> > >
> > > Thank you for asking. The pixel values output from cameras/sensors normally is on Digital Numbers (8 bits channel normally are from 0 to 250). The most common analysis pathway is to transform DN to radiance by using the camera/sensor setups. For this, you need to check the manual of your platform and/or Google about the transformation equations for each band/wavelength/layer. Another solution is to contact directly the company that provided your sensor and asks for the formulas/equations.
> > >
> > > Normally for biological research, radiance values are transformed to reflectance values to compare experiments/genotypes. Reflectance is the ratio between the incidence radiance (e.g, from the Sun) compared to the radiance reflected from the surface (e.g., plants). The variation of reflectance observed among genotypes is used to evaluate/correlate with biomass, maturity, tolerance, resistance, yield, etc. To transform radiance to reflectance you can (1) have a reflectance sensor directly connected to your Phenotyping Platform (e.g., connected to the drone) or (2) the most common is to use a reflectance panel in the field on the same day and time that you collect the data/images. These panels have some materials with known reflectance (e.g., 40%, 60%, etc.) that are used to correct pixels values.
> > >
> > > You can read more about other methods in this paper: https://doi.org/10.3390/rs11161917
> > >
> > > Hope this can help you.
> > >
> > > All the best,
> > > Filipe

Just one point for your attention, your mosaic (Foto.tif) still on Digital Numbers (normally with pixels' values varying from 0 to 250). Before starting any analysis or extracting data, it's important to make the radiometric calibration first to get radiance and/or reflectance (biological meaning).

> > > > >

> > > > >
> > > > >

> > > > >                      fieldShape = EX1.Shape$fieldShape,

>
> If you want to keep the same CRS after drawing the shapefile you can use the following strategy:
>
> 1) Using "extentGIS=TRUE" on fieldRotate():
> source(system.file("extdata", "fieldRotate.R", package = "FIELDimageR"))
> EX1.Rotated<-fieldRotate(mosaic = EX1.Crop, theta = 2.3, extentGIS=TRUE)
>
> 2) Followed by informing the rotation angle "theta" on fieldShape():
> EX1.Shape<-fieldShape(mosaic = EX1.RemSoil, ncols = 14, nrows = 9,
>                                             fieldMap = fieldMap, fieldData = DataTable, ID = "Plot",
>                                             theta = 2.3)
> plotRGB(EX1.RemSoil$newMosaic)
> plot(EX1.Shape$fieldShape,add=T)
> plotRGB(EX1)
> plot(EX1.Shape$fieldShapeGIS,add=T)

> All the best,
> Filipe

messages.subject: Re: FIELDimageR: Estimation of plant height
messages.subject_clean: FIELDimageR: Estimation of plant height
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

The estimated plant height has the same unit of your DSM (Digital Surface Model), which is the output from the orthomosaicin step.

Normally DSM is in meters (m), but you need to check it in your image.

Use one of the following functions (crs or projection) to have an idea about resolution ( e.g., 0.0175 m x 0.0175 m = 1.75 cm x 1.75 cm):

library(raster)
Test<-raster(DSM.tif)
crs(Test)
projection(Test)
Test

Best,
Filipe

messages.body_plain:
Hi Imran Khan,

To calculate indices as NDVI or NDRE it is necessary a multispectral image/mosaic (with RedEdge and/or NIR bands besides the traditional RGB). First, you need to inform the function fieldIndex() which layer in your mosaic represents the RedEdge (e.g., layer 4 in the mosaic) and NIR (e.g., layer 5 in the mosaic). Then on the parameter "index", you can write any index (e.g., NDVI and NDRE) from the table available in this link: https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P6

Here is an example of code to calculate NDVI and NDRE:

EX1.Indices<- fieldIndex(mosaic = EX1.RemSoil$newMosaic,
                                            Red=1,Green=2,Blue=3,

                                            RedEdge=4,
                                            NIR=5,
                                            index = c("NGRDI","BGI","NDVI","NDRE"))

Also, there is more information about multispectral in this link: https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P14

Best,
Filipe

Imran,

You need to inform which bands are the RedEdge and NIR. The easy solution, if you have a multispectral image (5 bands order: R, G, B, RedEdge, and NIR), is to include RedEdge=4 and NIR=5 in the function fieldIndex().

EX1.Indices<- fieldIndex(mosaic = EX1.RemSoil$newMosaic,
                                            Red=1,
                                            Green=2,
                                            Blue=3,
                                            RedEdge=4,
                                            NIR=5,
                                            index = c("NGRDI","BGI","NDVI","NDRE"))

Best,
Filipe

messages.body_plain:
Imran,
The number (e.g., 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5) in front of the band's name in the function fieldIndex() means the sequence of those bands in your picture. Imagine a multispectral image with 5 bands (e.g, Red, Green, Blue, RedEdge, and NIR) each band is represented for example by:

Red=1
Green=2
Blue=3
RedEdge=4
NIR=5

Where Red=1 means that the first layer/band of your multispectral image (with 5 layers) represents the region RED (e.g., 600-680 nm) of the spectrum capture by your sensor/camera.  Green=2 means the region GREEN (e.g., 480-600 nm). Blue=3 means the region BLUE (e.g., 400-480 nm). RedEdge=4 means the region RED-EDGE (e.g., 680-750 nm). And NIR=5 means the region NIR (e.g., >750 nm).

Hope it makes sense.

Best,
Filipe

messages.body_plain:
Hi Imran,

Unfortunately, you can’t calculate NDVI.

 The image that you shared is an RGB image with three layers (Red, Green, and Blue). To calculate NDVI or NDRE you need a Multispectral image with Red-Edge and NIR layers besides the RGB.

 Here, there are some nice reviews to help you to understand the difference:

·       https://doi.org/10.3389/fpls.2017.01111

·       https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tplants.2013.09.008

·       https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tplants.2018.11.007

 Using FIELDimageR and your image you can calculate other RGB indices as “BI”, “SCI”, “GLI”, “HI”, “NGRDI”, “SI”, “VARI”, “HUE”, and “BGI” (https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P6). For example, using the code below:

### START ###

 library(FIELDimageR)

library(raster)

EX1<-stack("EX6_RGB.JPG")

plotRGB(EX1)

EX1.Indices<- fieldIndex(mosaic = EX1, Red = 1, Green = 2, Blue = 3, index = c("NGRDI","BGI"))

 ### END ###

Hope this explanation helps you.

Best,

Filipe

messages.body_plain:
Hi Raffaele,

Thank you for contacting us. Normally, it happens when the shapefile's limits are outside the image. In other words, the shapefile is selecting an empty space with NAs. To fix this problem you can use the parameter na.rm = T. For example:

EX1.count <- fieldCount(mosaic = mask,
                        fieldShape = shapefile,
                        n.core = 4,
                        na.rm = T)

Let us know if it worked for you.
All the best,
Filipe

Hello Filpe,
thanks a lot for your prompt response. Yes, by removing NAs with na.rm=T it works ! Sorry, I didn't know it could be used inside the FieldCount function...

I take the chance of asking a clarification on the minSize argument. I understand from your tutorial that it is expressed as a % of the plot area, right?
I wonder what strategy would be the best, when processing a large batch of different images...
Thanks again for your great work.
Cheers
Raffaele

messages.subject: Re: fieldCount error in distmap(mask)
messages.subject_clean: fieldCount error in distmap(mask)
messages.body_plain:
Raffaele,

I am glad that it worked.

The minSize is used to tell the software which objects to ignore from your list of selected objects based on size.

The better approach is to use the basic pipeline with the default parameter. In this case, you should choose one image as an example and adjust the minSize by checking the outputs on $objectSel and $objectReject. Based on those object values you can set a threshold from where small objects will be transferred from Selected to Rejected.

The selected is your final results. There is more information in this link: https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P7

After you define your pipeline for one image (as an example), you can make a loop or parallel for all images following the code example in this link: https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P19

Let me know if you have more questions.

All the best,

Filipe

messages.subject: Imagem escurecendo
messages.subject_clean: Imagem escurecendo
messages.body_plain:
Olá, Felipe!

Estou tendo um problema ao utilizar o pacote, o qual nunca tive antes. Ficarei grato se puder me ajudar.

Tenho uma imagem em formato .tif (anexa) que pré processei no ArcGIS. Quando ploto ela com a função plotRGB(), ela é exibida normalmente, como abaixo:

EX1<-stack("CAIXAS_CLARAS_TODAS.tif")
plotRGB(EX1, r = 1, g = 2, b = 3)

Porém, quando começo os procedimentos de cortar a imagem com a função fieldCrop() e demais funções, a cor da imagem é alterada (escurecida), afetando os valores dos índices.

Tive este semelhante problema ao fazer um "clip" no ArcGIS, a imagem também estava escurecendo, mas desativei as alterações de estatísticas ao fazer um "clip" em imagens raster.

Conseguiria me ajudar neste problema? Agradeço desde já.

Abraços,
Igor

messages.subject: Re: Imagem escurecendo
messages.subject_clean: Imagem escurecendo
messages.body_plain:
Oi Igor,

 Obrigado por perguntar. Esse erro e novo pra mim...!

 Geralmente quando a imagem e muito grande e pesada essa mudança de cores pode acontecer no momento da plotagem (após o fieldCrop). No entanto, não quer dizer que muda o valor do pixel per se, muda apenas a escala de cores do plotRGB, uma vez que muitos outros pixels foram eliminados (função plotRGB do pacote raster balanceia os valores dos pixels).

 Poderia responder algumas perguntas para tentar entender o que está acontecendo:

 Qual versão do FIELDimageR você tem?
Você tentou fazer diferentes tamanhos de corte para ver o efeito no plotRGB?
Você tentou usar o plotRGB com o EX.Crop (a imagem cortada)?
Como você determinou que está mudando o valor dos índices? Gostaria de saber como você fez essa comparação de valores?

 Obrigado,

Filipe

messages.body_plain:
Obrigado, Felipe.
Respondendo as perguntas:

1. Estou utilizando a versão 0.2.1;
2. A imagem na função plotRGB está saindo em cores reais, em qualquer tamanho;
3. Quando uso plotRGB com o EX.Crop a imagem aparece em cores reais também;
4. Penso que pode estar diferente o valor dos índices devido a outra análise que fiz há alguns meses, com a mesma imagem,
que tinha dado outros valores nos índices, mas principalmente nos valores das bandas, bem menores. Devido à variação de cor
no momento de execução das funções fieldRotate e fieldShape, pensei que algo pode ter alterado o valor dos índices. Quando comparo
com os valores das bandas no ArcGIS, os resultados também resultam diferentes (os mesmos da análise que fiz há uns meses).
